chunks: By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

When God, Mighty and Majestic, created the intellect, He made it speak. Then He said to it: Come forth. So it came forth. Then He said to it: Go back. So it went back. Then He said to it: By My glory and My majesty! I have not created any creation more beloved to Me than you, and I do not perfect you except in those whom I love. Surely, by you I command, by you I prohibit, by you I punish, and by you I reward.

key_terms.العقل: al-'Aql - the intellect or reason; the first of God's creations according to this tradition
key_terms.عزتي وجلالي: By My glory and majesty - a divine oath emphasizing the gravity of the statement

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about God creating the intellect (al-Aql) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This celebrated hadith describes the creation of the intellect (al-'aql) as the first of God's creations. God tests the intellect's obedience by commanding it to come forward and retreat, then declares it His most beloved creation, perfected only in those He loves. The four divine functions of commanding, prohibiting, punishing, and rewarding are all linked to the intellect, establishing it as the foundation of moral and legal responsibility in Islamic thought.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from al-`Ala' b. Ruzayn from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as). He said:

When Allah created the intellect, He interrogated it. Then, He said to it: Come forth. So, it came forth. Then, He said to it: Go back. So, it went back. Then, He said to it: By My glory and My majesty! I have not created a thing that is more beloved to Me than you. I do not perfect you except in those whom I love. Surely, by you I command, by you I prohibit, by you I punish, and by you I reward.
